conversation.user: What can you actually verify, and what should I confirm with BCIT?
conversation.advisor:
**What I can verify**

- This is an active, full-time, in-person certificate at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus. The 41-week, non-co-op curriculum covers refrigeration, HVAC design, installation, servicing, controls, and electrical fundamentals.
- The curriculum contains 23 required courses, including **HVAC 1114 – Apply Fundamentals of Refrigeration**, **HVAC 2110 – Design Refrigeration Systems**, and **HVAC 3102 – Design HVAC Distribution Systems**.
- Admission requirements include specified English and mathematics options plus the BCIT Mechanical Reasoning Trades Entry Assessment. Admission is first-qualified while space remains.
- Based on your stated international-applicant status, this program’s published rules make you ineligible because it is unavailable to international students.

**What to confirm with BCIT**

- Whether another HVAC-related program is currently open to international applicants.
- Whether your specific academic credentials meet BCIT equivalency standards.
- Current intake dates and space availability, since scheduled intakes can change.

[BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/heating-ventilation-air-conditioning-and-refrigeration-technician-certificate-full-time-2958cert/)

programs.program_name: Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician
programs.program_overview: The Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVAC and R) Technician certificate is a non co-op program which provides a foundation in heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration system design, installation and service. industry designs, builds, maintains and repairs essential indoor comfort and cooling systems. Delivery: in person. See details . As a result of the expanding markets for refrigeration and air conditioning and changing technology, a dramatic need exists for qualified personnel both at home and abroad. Refrigeration equipment is used in supermarkets, and food processing and cold storage facilities, and sports facilities such as hockey and curling rinks, which are also a vital part of the industry. A Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic journeyperson fabricates, installs, alters, repairs/services any system used for cooling and/or heating (e.g. heat pumps) in closed systems that contain a refrigerant or a brine and thermoelectric cooling. This includes piping, controls and electrical work. These workers also connect rooftop units to gas and test and balance systems. The program The HVAC and R Technician certificate program is 41 weeks in duration combining classroom and shop instruction. After learning direct refrigeration systems, a broad range of topics focused on HVAC systems design, operation and controls are learned. Emphasis will be placed on diagnosis, service requirements and procedures. The first two levels of Gas B training is also included. (level 2 & 3). Who it’s for This career path is suited to those who are interested in designing, building, maintaining and repairing essential indoor comfort and cooling systems and who enjoy being independent, troubleshooting and and problem solving. What grads can do Graduates of this program who enter the trade within one year of graduation can expect to receive credit for three levels of technical training for the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic apprenticeship. Students are encouraged to return to Level 4 apprentice training (10 weeks) when appropriate to complete their level 4 training to qualify to write their Gas B ticket and prepare for the Interprovincial Red Seal certification exam. Next up Entrance Requirements
programs.notes: Program length 41 weeks, full-time Grading The course passing grade is 64 per cent. In order to successfully complete each level, a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 70 per cent is required. An overall GPA of 70 per cent is required to successfully complete the program. Accreditation Graduates of this program who enter the trade within one year of graduation can expect to receive credit for three levels of technical training for the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning apprenticeship. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Industry training authority BCIT transfers the student's name, contact information, Personal Education Number (PEN), and the name and date of the completed Foundation program to SkilledTradesBC. This information is used for the purposes of tracking successful completions in order to grant credit towards apprenticeship where applicable, and communicating with trainees to promote continuation in an apprenticeship program. program.program_name: Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Technician
program.program_overview: The Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (HVAC and R) Technician certificate is a non co-op program which provides a foundation in heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration system design, installation and service. industry designs, builds, maintains and repairs essential indoor comfort and cooling systems. Delivery: in person. See details . As a result of the expanding markets for refrigeration and air conditioning and changing technology, a dramatic need exists for qualified personnel both at home and abroad. Refrigeration equipment is used in supermarkets, and food processing and cold storage facilities, and sports facilities such as hockey and curling rinks, which are also a vital part of the industry. A Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic journeyperson fabricates, installs, alters, repairs/services any system used for cooling and/or heating (e.g. heat pumps) in closed systems that contain a refrigerant or a brine and thermoelectric cooling. This includes piping, controls and electrical work. These workers also connect rooftop units to gas and test and balance systems. The program The HVAC and R Technician certificate program is 41 weeks in duration combining classroom and shop instruction. After learning direct refrigeration systems, a broad range of topics focused on HVAC systems design, operation and controls are learned. Emphasis will be placed on diagnosis, service requirements and procedures. The first two levels of Gas B training is also included. (level 2 & 3). Who it’s for This career path is suited to those who are interested in designing, building, maintaining and repairing essential indoor comfort and cooling systems and who enjoy being independent, troubleshooting and and problem solving. What grads can do Graduates of this program who enter the trade within one year of graduation can expect to receive credit for three levels of technical training for the Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic apprenticeship. Students are encouraged to return to Level 4 apprentice training (10 weeks) when appropriate to complete their level 4 training to qualify to write their Gas B ticket and prepare for the Interprovincial Red Seal certification exam.
